references.text: Joshua had just conquered Makkedah, and this verse continues with the march onward to Libnah, showing the systematic conquest of the Canaanite cities.
Describes the same pattern of conquest as at Libnah, where Joshua and Israel move on to Lachish and defeat it.
Libnah is mentioned in the list of kings that Joshua defeated, confirming the conquest that began in this verse.
Libnah is listed as one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah, showing the result of the conquest.
Libnah was later given to the descendants of Aaron as a Levitical city, showing the city's importance after the conquest.
Libnah revolted against Judah during the reign of King Joram, showing the city's further history after Joshua's conquest.
Libnah is mentioned in connection with the Assyrian king Sennacherib's campaign, showing the city's continued strategic significance.
Parallel account of Sennacherib's siege of Libnah, confirming the city's ongoing military importance.
